dry-0.text: Saint Thomas-in-the-East, Jamaica. August eighteen sixty-five.

dry-6.text: Stony Gut, in the hills above Morant Bay.
dry-6.caption: Stony Gut, in the hills above Morant Bay.

dry-12.text: No rain for two years. The yams are small.
dry-12.caption: No rain for two years. The yams are small.

dry-18.text: Paul Bogle's yard. He is a deacon here.
dry-18.caption: Paul Bogle's yard. He is a deacon here.

dry-24.text: The chapel, thatched, where the village meets.
dry-24.caption: The chapel, thatched, where the village meets.

dry-30.text: Your house. Your family. You are Hannah.
dry-30.caption: Your house. Your family. You are Hannah.

walk-0.text: Spanish Town, the capital. Two days' walk from Stony Gut.
walk-0.caption: Spanish Town, the capital. Two days' walk from Stony Gut.

walk-7.text: The square. King's House, where the Governor lives.
walk-7.caption: The square. King's House, where the Governor lives.

walk-14.text: The men from Stony Gut wait in the sun.
walk-14.caption: The men from Stony Gut wait in the sun.

walk-20.text: They want only to be heard.
walk-20.caption: They want only to be heard.

home-6.text: Two days' walk home, with nothing.
home-6.caption: Two days' walk home, with nothing.

home-12.text: In Saint Thomas, people talk of nothing else.
home-12.caption: In St Thomas, people talk of nothing else.

meeting-6.text: One by one, men come up the path to the chapel.
meeting-6.caption: One by one, men come up the path to the chapel.

meeting-13.text: A lantern inside. The men speak low.
meeting-13.caption: A lantern inside. The men speak low.

meeting-18.text: Deacon Clarke has sent for you. You can write.
meeting-18.caption: Deacon Clarke has sent for you. You can write.

warrant-0.text: Tuesday the tenth of October eighteen sixty-five. Early morning.
warrant-0.caption: Tuesday 10 October 1865. Early morning.

warrant-5.text: Police come up the track with a warrant.
warrant-5.caption: Police come up the track with a warrant.

warrant-11.text: They have come to take Paul Bogle.
warrant-11.caption: They have come to take Paul Bogle.

warrant-21.text: Men come out of the chapel, out of the cane.
warrant-21.caption: Men come out of the chapel, out of the cane.

warrant-27.text: Now the police are the ones who are held.
warrant-27.caption: Now the police are the ones who are held.

bay-0.text: Morant Bay. Wednesday the eleventh of October eighteen sixty-five.
bay-0.caption: Morant Bay. Wednesday 11 October 1865.

bay-7.text: The court-house, with its row of arches.
bay-7.caption: The court-house, with its row of arches.

bay-13.text: The vestry sits inside. Volunteers stand guard.
bay-13.caption: The vestry sits inside. Volunteers stand guard.

bay-19.text: The market on the Parade, under the guinep tree.
bay-19.caption: The market on the Parade, under the guinep tree.

riot-0.text: Behind the stall. Between three and four o'clock.
riot-0.caption: Behind the stall. Between three and four o'clock.

riot-4.text: Shells and drums, from the east road.
riot-4.caption: Shells and drums, from the east road.

riot-10.text: Hundreds of people come onto the Parade.
riot-10.caption: Hundreds of people come onto the Parade.

riot-17.text: The Custos calls out: Peace, peace.
riot-17.caption: The Custos calls out: "Peace, peace."

riot-23.text: He begins to read the Riot Act. Stones fly.
riot-23.caption: He begins to read the Riot Act. Stones fly.

riot-29_9.text: You hide your eyes. People run.
riot-29_9.caption: You hide your eyes. People run.

riot-45.text: The fire spreads to the court-house. It grows dark.
riot-45.caption: The fire spreads to the court-house. It grows dark.

soldiers-0.text: Wednesday the eighteenth of October eighteen sixty-five.
soldiers-0.caption: Wednesday 18 October 1865.

soldiers-11.text: People run for the cane and the hills.
soldiers-11.caption: People run for the cane and the hills.

soldiers-17.text: Gran pulls you behind the house.
soldiers-17.caption: Gran pulls you behind the house.

burning-0.text: Thursday the nineteenth of October. From the cave mouth.
burning-0.caption: Thursday 19 October. From the cave mouth.

burning-11_5.text: Then Mister Bogle's house. Then yours.
burning-11_5.caption: Then Mr Bogle's house. Then yours.

burning-27.text: Soldiers lead men away. One wears a hat like Papa's.
burning-27.caption: Soldiers lead men away. One wears a hat like Papa's.

courts-0.text: Morant Bay, late October eighteen sixty-five.
courts-0.caption: Morant Bay, late October 1865.

courts-6.text: The court-house is a burnt shell. A shed is the court now.
courts-6.caption: The court-house is a burnt shell. A shed is the court now.

courts-13.text: Officers judge. Prisoners wait on the benches.
courts-13.caption: Officers judge. Prisoners wait on the benches.

courts-19.text: Behind the shed, a man is tied to a post.
courts-19.caption: Behind the shed, a man is tied to a post.

courts-22.text: Mama turns your face away. You hear it.
courts-22.caption: Mama turns your face away. You hear it.

dawn-7.text: Far along the shore, a frame of dark timber.
dawn-7.caption: Far along the shore, a frame of dark timber.

dawn-14.text: At Morant Bay, George William Gordon was hanged on the twenty-third of October.
dawn-14.caption: At Morant Bay, George William Gordon was hanged on 23 October.

dawn-20.text: Paul Bogle was hanged at Morant Bay too.
dawn-20.caption: Paul Bogle was hanged at Morant Bay too.

dawn-26.text: Both are National Heroes of Jamaica today.
dawn-26.caption: Both are National Heroes of Jamaica today.

today-6.text: The court-house was rebuilt after eighteen sixty-five. It burned in two thousand and seven.
today-6.caption: The court-house was rebuilt after 1865. It burned in 2007.

today-12.text: Edna Manley's statue of Paul Bogle stood here from nineteen sixty-five.
today-12.caption: Edna Manley's statue of Paul Bogle stood here from 1965.

today-16.text: It was taken down to be mended after the fire.
today-16.caption: It was taken down to be mended after the fire.

today-20.text: Paul Bogle and George William Gordon are National Heroes of Jamaica.
today-20.caption: Paul Bogle and George William Gordon are National Heroes of Jamaica.

today-24.text: Thousands of others have no statue. Their names are in the record.
today-24.caption: Thousands of others have no statue. Their names are in the record.
